correctness.rationale: For n>=2 the ballot definition is permutation invariant. Fix k ones, move them first, and map each remaining preference to q=max(1,a-k); this is a bijection with a PF_(n-k) word and k possible preimages of q=1. Marking just preference 2 gives weight k-1+v. Using the established A_m(t)=t(t+m)^(m-1) produces the bivariate enumerator exactly, including k=n. Dividing by the k-fiber count yields a Bernoulli-plus-binomial conditional PGF; nested coupling proves strict stochastic regression. Differentiation/integration of the shifted-binomial first marginal yields the exact covariance and 2/e-1 limit. The all-size proof covers every k and n>=2; a standalone verifier independently checked 5,026 finite assertions, not as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The established one-value marginal and the lucky-car enumerators are not claimed new. Relevant primary sections of Diaconis-Hicks, Kenyon-Yin, and Stanley-Yin were compared at the level of random variables, exact formula and implication; their displayed results count first-value preferences, unluckiness, other same-preference classes or car-index coordinates, not the new two fixed preference-value occupancy law with strict conditional ordering and limiting covariance. Targeted public-record and literature searches did not return a stronger matching statement. Broader multivariate enumerators and historical priority remain qualified risks.
residual_risks: Classical general multivariate parking-function preference enumerators or chapter-level formulas not inspected in full could contain a stronger specialization or already imply the same evaluated two-value identity.
A plausible exact table of first-two occupancy multiplicities could exist outside the queried indices; failed search is not a uniqueness certificate.
The inspected sections are not entire corpora; historical priority and independent validation remain unperformed.

value.rationale: The number of cars requesting the first two spots is a natural local occupancy profile of the linear-probing/parking model. The complete conditional distribution reveals a strict stochastic negative-regression hierarchy across every possible number of first-spot requests; the exact covariance converges to 2/e-1 rather than disappearing as in independent sparse occupancy. These structural and asymptotic conclusions are sharper than a one-value marginal, a finite exercise, or a reparameterization of the lucky-car statistic.
